newsitem.title: USA: Dollar rallies on Greenspan interest rate talk.
newsitem.headline: Dollar rallies on Greenspan interest rate talk.

text.p: The dollar ended broadly higher Thursday after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan gave his clearest warning yet that U.S. interest rates might be raised for the first time in almost two years.
The strong gains easily wiped out earlier losses that came following a report showing the U.S. trade deficit widened to its highest level in nearly a decade.

Testifying before a joint committee of Congress, Greenspan said the economy has "a great deal a vigor" and said strength in the job market could lead to higher inflation. He said the central bank must look beyond the current rosy economic data when setting monetary policy because the effects of any changes in rates might not be felt for a year or more.
Some analysts read his comments as a strong hint that the Fed could raise short-term interest rates when the central bank's policy committee meets Tuesday.
"He raised the possibility of a Fed tightening ... and that helped underpin the dollar," said Rick Gomes, foreign exchange manager at Republic National Bank of New York.
The dollar tends to benefit from increases in interest rates because higher rates make U.S.-denominated assets more attractive to foreign investors.
The dollar climbed against the mark to settle at 1.6930, compared with its close on Wednesday at 1.6803.
Against the yen, the dollar rose to 123.75 at the close, compared with 122.82.

The dollar had tumbled at the opening after the Commerce Department reported the January U.S. trade gap shot up 21.1 percent to a larger-than-expected $12.71 billion. But strong demand easily wiped out losses later in the session.
"The dollar had been weaker and the move down was caused by the trade data. But when Greenspan started commenting, it went off to the races," said Bob Near, vice president at the Bank of New York.

The deficit also raised some fears of trade frictions. The U.S. deficit with Japan edged up 0.7 percent to $4.29 bilion in January while the politically sensitive trade gap with China surged by 40.8 percent to $3.72 billion.
There was no overnight trading in Tokyo due to the Vernal Equinox public holiday in Japan, which closed Tokyo's financial markets.
The British pound weakened against the dollar, slipping to close at $1.5935 from $1.5982 on Wednesday.
The dollar moved higher against the Swiss franc to close at 1.4535 compared with Wednesday's close at 1.4425. It settled at Canadian $1.3796 compared with C$1.3774.
